issues.description: Unreachable break after raise makes loop exit after first axis only via exception, but logic is also wrong for multi-axis arrays
issues.detail: The `break` after `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is dead code. More importantly, the loop only raises on the first offending axis, but `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * itemsize` computes the total shard volume regardless of which axis triggered, which may be misleading. Also, raising inside the loop before checking other axes is fine, but the dead `break` shows confused intent.

issues.description: Raising PerformanceWarning as an exception is a breaking behavior change, not a warning
issues.detail: `PerformanceWarning` is a Warning subclass but the code uses `raise`, turning a warning into a hard failure. Users with `array.chunk-size` smaller than the shard who previously got data written (perhaps unsafely) will now get an exception. The PR description even asks whether an exception is appropriate — this needs explicit decision and a deprecation path, or use `warnings.warn` instead.

issues.description: Test uses pytest.raises on PerformanceWarning instead of pytest.warns, masking the API question
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` is named `_warns` but asserts `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. This codifies the raise-as-exception behavior in tests without addressing whether warning semantics are correct. If maintainers later switch to `warnings.warn`, the test will need updating; the name/behavior mismatch is confusing.

issues.description: Operator precedence bug risk: `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0`
issues.detail: Python evaluates this as `not ((nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) == 0)` which happens to be correct, but it is fragile and hard to read. Prefer `nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0` for clarity. A future edit could easily break this by misreading precedence.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation may be wrong when zarr_write_chunks contains multiple axes
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks)` multiplies tuples of tuples — `zarr_write_chunks` comes from `_get_zarr_write_chunks(z)` which returns the shard/chunk shape as a tuple of ints per axis. The product gives shard element count; multiplied by itemsize gives bytes per shard. For multi-dim arrays this is correct, but only the failing-axis size may be more informative. Also np.prod of an empty tuple returns 1.0; verify dtype handling.

issues.description: Only checks dw[0] — assumes all chunk sizes in axis are equal
issues.detail: `nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` only inspects the first chunk size along each axis. `normalize_chunks` with auto can produce uneven trailing chunks; while the leading chunk being shard-aligned is what matters for writes, the comment/error message implies all chunks are checked. Consider documenting this assumption or checking the max chunk size.

review.summary: The PR's main correctness issue is that it `raise`s `PerformanceWarning` rather than warning, converting a previously-soft condition into a hard failure with no deprecation path — and the PR description itself flags this as an open question. There is a dead `break` statement after the raise, and `not x % y == 0` should be rewritten as `x % y != 0` for clarity. The test name says "warns" but uses `pytest.raises`, locking in the raise semantics before the design question is resolved. The shard-multiple rechunking logic itself is sensible; the issues are around the warning/exception API decision and a few small code-clarity bugs.
